Move or rename a page without breaking the links people already have, and choose what readers see on a URL with no page.

List moved pages under redirects: at the top level of aiui.yaml: Key Meaning source A site path starting with /. :name matches one path segment; a final :name* matches the rest of the path, including nothing (/docs/v1/:slug* matches /docs/v1 and /docs/v1/a/b). destination A site path or a full URL. It can reuse the names from source. permanent true (default) answers with 301, false with 302. The first matching rule wins. Leave out the --base-path prefix: rules use site paths and the build adds the base path.

aiui build publishes every rule whose source is not a published page: Host Exact source (/docs/old) Wildcard source (/docs/v1/:slug*) aiui serve 301 / 302 301 / 302 (a file at the path wins) Netlify, Cloudflare Pages 301 / 302 from the _redirects file 301 / 302 from _redirects GitHub Pages, any static host A stub page at the old URL (meta refresh, a canonical link, a script redirect) The docs app follows the rule from the page-not-found view The query string and the #section carry over unless the destination sets its own. A stub never replaces a real file; it has noindex and a canonical link to the new URL. The link check treats every source as a valid link.
aiui validate warns when an exact rule loops or ends at a docs path with no page (7010), or when a page is still published at its source (7011).

A URL with no page shows "Page not found", a link home, the search, and up to three pages from the sidebar whose names are close to the URL (a typo such as /docs/instalation offers Installation), unless a redirects: rule matches first.
